name: Question 15
problem:
Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a $3\times 3$ matrix $A$ in the given order:

$$
{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1},\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1}
$$

What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?
worked_solution:
First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

- The first operation is ${R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

- The second operation is ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

- The third operation is ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1}.$ The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={E}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix $A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{1}$ on the left and get ${E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to ${E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{2}$ on the left and get ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}A,$ we multiply by ${E}_{3}$ on the left and get ${E}_{3}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}A:$ 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot A
$$

Suppose that the following elementary row operations are applied to a 3×3 matrix A in the given order: R2↔R3,R3:=R3+2R1,R2:=R2−2R1 What is the equivalent notation in terms of matrix multiplication?

a
[10001−2001]⋅[100210001]⋅[100001010]⋅A
b
[100010−201]⋅[100010201]⋅[100011010]⋅A
c
[100210001]⋅[100010−201]⋅[101001010]⋅A
d
[100−210001]⋅[100010201]⋅[100001010]⋅A
e
[100−210001]⋅[102010001]⋅[001100010]⋅A
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's find the elementary matrices corresponding to the given elementary row operations.

  • The first operation is R2↔R3. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R2↔R3∼[100001010]=E1

  • The second operation is R3:=R3+2R1. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R3:=R3+2R1∼[100010201]=E2

  • The third operation is R2:=R2−2R1. The corresponding elementary matrix can be found by applying this same elementary row operation to the identity matrix as follows: I=[100010001]R2:=R2−2R1∼[100−210001]=E3

To apply the first elementary row operation to the matrix A, we multiply by E1 on the left and get E1A:

[100001010]⋅A

Then, to apply the second elementary row operation to E1A, we multiply by E2 on the left and get E2E1A:

[100010201]⋅[100001010]⋅A

Finally, to apply the third elementary row operation to E2E1A, we multiply by E3 on the left and get E3E2E1A:

[100−210001]⋅[100010201]⋅[100001010]⋅A
